title: Bootstrap Introduction
summary: Bootstrap is a set of ready-made page styles. Learn how class names can style a button, add space and build a card.
introduction: Imagine making a poster with ready-cut shapes. You still choose the words and layout, but the shapes save time. Bootstrap works in a similar way for web pages. It gives you CSS styles to reuse. You choose them by adding class names to your HTML.
learningObjectives: Explain what Bootstrap adds to HTML and CSS
Choose Bootstrap classes for a button and a card
Tell which page jobs need more than Bootstrap

blocks.text: These examples need the Bootstrap 5 CSS file. The [setup lesson](/tutorials/bootstrap/setup) shows how to add it to a page. They are shown as code here because the plain HTML playground does not load Bootstrap for you. You can read the result without installing anything yet.

blocks.code:
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">
  Read a story
</button>
blocks.title: A Bootstrap button

blocks.content: With Bootstrap CSS loaded, the page shows a button with the main theme colour.

blocks.text: `btn` gives the button its basic shape and spacing. `btn-primary` chooses the main colour. Bootstrap 5 uses blue by default, but a site can change its theme. A class changes the look; it does not give this button a new job when clicked.

blocks.code:
Our reading club

We read one story each week.
blocks.title: A page with some breathing room

blocks.text: `container` holds the page content and limits its width on larger screens. `p-3` adds space inside the box. The `p` means padding. The number 3 is a step on Bootstrap's spacing scale, not 3 pixels.

blocks.code:
Book of the week

A story about a trip to the moon.
blocks.title: A small book card

blocks.text: A **card** is a box that groups related things. `card` adds the outer card style. `card-body` adds space inside it. The heading and paragraph tell the reader about one book.

rows: A name in HTML that CSS can use to choose a style.
A ready-made page part, such as a card or a menu.
A small class with one job, such as `p-3` for space.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Adding a class name is not enough on its own. Your page must load the matching Bootstrap CSS. Parts such as menus that open and close also need Bootstrap's JavaScript.
Bootstrap helps with styles and some page controls. It does not store your data or decide how your whole app works. Those jobs need your own code. This learning site itself works without an account.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Find the words a reader will see in each example. Then change the card to describe your favourite hobby. Keep the class names the same.

seo.title: Bootstrap Introduction – What It Is and Why Use It
seo.description: Learn what Bootstrap 5.3 is, what Reboot, components and utilities give every page, what the framework is not, and how to spot Bootstrap 3 and 4 code.
